relatedSnapshot.title: Locked out of the Acquisity dashboard after an account suspension pending a finance review
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom source: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: On 2026-09-27 the customer wrote that she is locked out of her Slack, Acquisity dashboard, and Heartbeat, said "finance blocked me", asked repeatedly for a human, and then asked for goodwill access to at least Slack and the Acquisity dashboard while a finance matter is cleared, saying she has already sent receipts. A support admin asked whether she wanted to remove a workspace; she said the opposite.

Finding: her workspace owner account was suspended by an admin on 2026-09-25 with the reason "CB - <chargeback> - $525.01 - SI $700". Signing in with that account is refused with the suspension reason, which is exactly the dashboard lockout she reports. She then registered a second account with a different email on 2026-09-27, which has no workspace, and reached support through it. Her owner membership on the workspace is intact and the workspace itself is not deleted, so lifting the suspension restores her access; nothing else on the workspace is broken. Slack and Heartbeat are separate platforms with their own access, so the Acquisity suspension does not explain those lockouts; that part is unverified from Acquisity side.

Human decision needed: the team that owns the finance matter should confirm the status of that chargeback and decide whether to lift the suspension. If it is lifted, she signs in again with her original workspace email.

Testable claim: The customer's workspace owner account is suspended in the product, so sign-in is refused and the dashboard is inaccessible; restoring access requires an admin to lift that suspension.

relatedSnapshot.title: Acquisity access blocked after Name 1 campaign, plan shows Basic
relatedSnapshot.description:
User reports being blocked from proceeding in Cold Email Agent and SDR due to "Acquisity integration required" and a prompt to join Acquisity again for $185 while starting a second email campaign.

The account previously ran a full campaign during Name 1 with Acquisity and AI SDR active (statuses like "AI replied" and "escalated" were shown). Now the workspace is showing on the Basic plan, which does not include Cold Email Agent or AI SDR, even though the user believes they should still have access from their Name 1 setup.

This needs investigation into why the workspace plan/entitlements reverted to Basic after the first campaign and why the UI is still surfacing Acquisity and SDR flows but blocking progress behind an "integration required" and upgrade/paywall state.

Please review this workspace's subscription history, Launchpad-related access, and Acquisity/Cold Email Agent entitlements to confirm whether the current plan is correct and ensure the UI and access state are consistent.

relatedSnapshot.description:

Recommended change is to fail open when Autumn errors so paid users are not locked out during provider outages. See Autumn docs.

relatedSnapshot.title: Deleting a client workspace wipes the owner's entire Acquisity account
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

A customer deleted a client workspace ("Company Five") and the platform deleted the **owner's entire Acquisity account**, not just the workspace. The owner is locked out right now and needs manual account reinstatement today.

This is a destructive cascade-delete bug: workspace deletion should never remove the owner account / other workspaces.

## Name 8 signal

* Name 8 topic: `<uuid>`
* Severity: High | Confidence: 0.92 | Track: Engineering
* New (1 customer today), but data-loss impact is severe and immediate.

## Why new

No open ticket tracks workspace-deletion cascading into owner-account deletion. Related prior work: ENG-9948 (manual restore of workspaces/access for Name 6 — suggests this class of incident has happened before), ENG-1467 (restrict Member-role workspace deletion), ENG-5851 (billing cleanup on deletion). None address the account-wipe cascade.

## Immediate action

Company Five owner needs manual account reinstatement today (support/ops).

## Source

* Name 4

relatedSnapshot.title: Password reset emails not delivered to user (accepted by provider, never landing) — <email>
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Unconfirmed (email deliverability issue; the reset flow itself works)

## Evidence

* Customer Name 12 Name 10 (user id `<uuid>`, email `<email>`) cannot log in and never receives the password reset email. Reported via Intercom.
* Prod DB (read-only): account healthy — `email_verified=true`, not banned, credential account with password present. 4 reset-password verification tokens generated today for this user (00:16, 00:19, 01:18, 01:42 UTC), so Name 9 reset flow generates links correctly.
* Axiom: no email-send errors around those timestamps → Resend accepted the sends (no `EmailSendError` thrown).
* The recipient mailbox works and is actively receiving OTHER Acquisity mail (AI SDR escalation notifications, etc.) — see screenshots in the Intercom thread. AI SDR escalation emails go through the same `emailService`/Resend sender (`env.EMAIL_FROM`) as the password reset email, yet the reset email specifically never lands.
* Pattern (provider accepts the send, mail never delivered, to an address that receives our other mail) most strongly suggests the recipient is on Resend's suppression/bounce list. Could not verify directly — no Resend credentials available in the investigation session.

## Second issue found

* CS attempted to change the account email to `<email>`, but the change did NOT persist — `user.email` is still `<email>` and `user.updated_at` is `2026-06-13` (unchanged). So the 'change email + resend' retest actually still sent to `<email>`; `<email>` never received a reset. Needs confirmation whether the admin email-change flow requires user confirmation (by design) or silently failed.

## What's needed to resolve

1. Check Resend suppression/bounce list for `<email>` (and `<email>`); remove suppression if present and resend.
2. Investigate why the admin email change did not persist.
3. Immediate customer unblock (separate from root cause): admin sets a temporary password directly so the user can log in without email.

## Links

* Intercom: <url:app.intercom.com>
* Slack thread: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
* Name 11 session: <url>

relatedSnapshot.title: Banned user still has an active Pro subscription billing $185/month
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Intercom conversation

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Context

Customer Name 18 Name 19 (Company Six) asked to cancel their Acquisity subscription. Support directed them to Settings > Billing > Cancel Subscription, but the customer could not log in because their account is banned. Support also cannot impersonate the banned account.

## Claim

A banned Acquisity user still has an active Pro subscription billing $185/month, because banning a user blocks app access but does not cancel their Autumn/Stripe subscription, so recurring billing continues while they are locked out.

## Evidence

* user.banned = true, ban_reason = "RR" (refund request), no expiry.
* Autumn: active Pro subscription, $185/month, current period 2026-08-19 to 2026-09-19.
* Stripe: active subscription, next charge ~2026-09-19.
* Root cause matches ENG-10782 (banned/offboarded users can still have active Autumn/Stripe billing).
